scope: Cumulative vocabulary flashcard plural/conjugation extraction (541/754 detailed cards across 45 lessons), WCAG 2.1 SC 3.1.2 lang="de" & W3C bidi dir="auto" markup, audio/TTS playback exclusivity, and deterministic WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 color-contrast backgrounds across 231 screen states

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 3.1.2: Language of Parts (Level AA) | WAI | W3C
sources.takeaway: WCAG 2.1 SC 3.1.2 (Level AA) and Technique H58 require marking passages or phrases in a different language with the HTML lang attribute (lang="de") so screen readers and braille translators apply German pronunciation rules instead of the page default Arabic (lang="ar").

sources.title: Declaring language in HTML — W3C Internationalization
sources.takeaway: W3C I18n guidance on declaring default page language on <html> and wrapping foreign-language words/phrases in inline or block elements with BCP 47 language tags (lang="de") while keeping Arabic UI attributes separate.

sources.title: Plural Nouns in German Grammar — Lingolia
sources.takeaway: German plural formation patterns (-n/-en, -e, -r/-er, -s, no ending, umlaut changes, and singularia/pluralia tantum such as die Milch, das Obst, die Eltern) matching the 517 plural/conjugation entries surfaced across A1.2–B2.12.

sources.title: Präsens – Present Tense in German Grammar — Lingolia
sources.takeaway: German present-tense conjugation and stem-vowel changes (e->i/ie, a->ä, modal verbs) matching the verb conjugation notes in the A1–B2 vocabulary tables.
